progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: chem-m7-c01 (drawing and naming hydrocarbons up to C8; saturated and unsaturated; the zigzag), chem-m7-c02 (structural isomers; butane and 2-methylpropane, with their boiling points shown but not explained). Year 11: covalent bonds as shared electron pairs; intermolecular forces (dispersion forces, hydrogen bonding) and that stronger attractions between molecules raise the boiling point; polar and non-polar molecules. Not assumed: VSEPR by name, bond angles, the words tetrahedral, trigonal planar, linear, homologous series, general formula, intramolecular. Scene 2 explains the repulsion idea in one sentence rather than relying on Year 11 shape work.
progression.startsWith: Build single, double and triple bond models. The video opens: The gas in this camping stove is mostly butane, four carbons long, and it boils near minus one degree. Candle wax is made of the same kind of molecule, alkanes, but each chain has twenty or more carbons, and it's a solid at room temperature. Same family, very different substances.
progression.stopsAfter: stating and explaining the shape and bond angle at a carbon with a single, double or triple bond; building and writing members of the alkane, alkene and alkyne series up to C8 with their general formulas and functional groups; telling a homologous series from isomers; explaining boiling point trends with chain length, branching and between series of equal size, using intramolecular and intermolecular bonding; explaining hydrocarbon solubility in water and in non-polar solvents. No dataset processing (chem-m7-p01), no reactions (chem-m7-c04a), no orbital names.
progression.nextLesson: process real boiling point data across the alkane series (route chem-m7-p01, "Investigate a hydrocarbon homologous series"); the weaker second bond returns in chem-m7-c04a.

teaching.task: Butane is a gas and candle wax is a solid, yet both are made of the same kind of molecule. How does carbon's bonding set a hydrocarbon's shape, and how do size and shape set its boiling point and solubility?
teaching.causalExplanation: (1) the same kind of molecule can be a gas or a solid (1); (2) bonding electron groups push apart, so four single bonds give a tetrahedral carbon and chains zigzag (2); (3) a double bond gives three directions, so a flat carbon, and its second bond is weaker and exposed (3); (4) a triple bond gives two directions, so a linear carbon; shape is read carbon by carbon (4); (5) adding CH₂ builds a homologous series with one general formula (5); (6) each multiple bond removes two hydrogens, giving the alkene and alkyne formulas; shared bonding (the same functional group, or for alkanes single bonds only) means shared reactions, and size changes the physical properties gradually (6); (7) series members differ by CH₂, isomers share a formula (7); (8) boiling separates molecules but keeps every covalent bond, so boiling point measures the forces between molecules (8); (9) longer chains have more electrons and more contact, so stronger dispersion forces and higher boiling points (9); (10) tetrahedral carbons make a straight chain zigzag so it can lie alongside its neighbours, while branches reduce contact, so weaker forces and lower boiling points (10); (11) the bond type barely changes the forces when the size is the same (11); (12) hydrocarbons would break water's hydrogen bonds without replacing them, so they stay separate, but they mix with other hydrocarbons (12); memory aid (13); two attempts and brief feedback (14 to 17); handoff (18); key notes (19).
teaching.conversationalApproach: butane in a camping stove boils near minus one degree while candle wax, made of the same kind of molecule, is a solid, so the video asks how carbon's bonding explains the difference. Shape is taught carbon by carbon from the number of bonding directions (four give tetrahedral at about 109.5 degrees, three give trigonal planar at about 120, two give linear at 180), with propene showing that shape belongs to each carbon. The alkanes then line up as a homologous series differing by CH2, with general formulas for alkanes, alkenes and alkynes (open chain, one multiple bond), and a series is separated from a set of isomers. Properties follow from strong covalent bonds inside molecules against weak dispersion forces between them: longer chains have more electrons and more contact so they boil higher, branched isomers touch less so they boil lower, chain length matters more than bond type between series, and hexane forms a layer on water because it cannot replace the hydrogen bonds it would break, while it mixes with heptane. The memory aid counts directions at each carbon and contact between molecules. Two exam questions follow with brief feedback.
teaching.openingDecision: The gas in this camping stove is mostly butane, four carbons long, and it boils near minus one degree. Candle wax is made of the same kind of molecule, alkanes, but each chain has twenty or more carbons, and it's a solid at room temperature. Same family, very different substances. So how does carbon's bonding explain the difference?
teaching.understandingCheck: (A1) "Propyne has the condensed structural formula CH₃C≡CH. (a) State the shape and bond angle around each carbon atom. (b) Identify the homologous series to which propyne belongs, and show that its molecular formula fits the general formula of that series." Tests shapes carbon by carbon and the general formula. Crossed mistake: "all three carbons linear" (site lesson 4 MC distractor). (A2) "Hexane and 2,3-dimethylbutane both have the molecular formula C₆H₁₄. Explain which compound has the higher boiling point, with reference to the intramolecular and intermolecular bonding present." Skeletal formulas shown beside the names. New compounds (C₆ instead of the site's C₅); uses the syllabus wording "intramolecular and intermolecular". Crossed mistake: "the branched molecule has weaker covalent bonds" (site card 4 Critical Error).
teaching.curriculumScope: Syllabus (NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017), as printed: "construct models, identify the functional group, and write structural and molecular formulae for homologous series of organic chemical compounds, up to C8 (ACSCH035) :; alkanes; alkenes; alkynes" "analyse the shape of molecules formed between carbon atoms when a single, double or triple bond is formed between them" "explain the properties within and between the homologous series of alkanes with reference to the intermolecular and intramolecular bonding present" this video starts from bond models (single, double and triple) and stops at predicting boiling point and solubility trends across hydrocarbon series. It teaches: four bonding directions around a carbon spread as far apart as possible, so a carbon with four single bonds is tetrahedral (about 109.5°), which is why c01's chains zigzag; a carbon in a C=C has three bonding directions (the double bond counts as one), so it is trigonal planar (about 120°); the second bond of a double bond lies above and below the line between the carbons and is weaker (named here only as "the second bond", a forward link to chem-m7-c04a); a carbon in a C≡C has two directions, so it is linear (180°); shape belongs to each carbon, not the whole molecule (propene); homologous series (members built the same way, with the same functional group if they have one, each differing by CH₂), constructed as models up to C8; general formulas CnH2n+2, CnH2n and CnH2n−2 for open chains (no ring) and why each multiple bond removes two hydrogens; members of a series react alike while physical properties change gradually; homologous series against isomers (c02 callback); intramolecular (covalent bonds inside a molecule) against intermolecular (dispersion forces between molecules) and why boiling breaks only the second; boiling point rises with chain length (more electrons, more contact); branching lowers boiling point (less contact); between series of equal carbon number, boiling points are close, and chain length matters more; hydrocarbons barely dissolve in water but mix with non-polar solvents, explained by which attractions are broken and replaced. Not here: processing and evaluating the full boiling point dataset, graphing it, and the limits of the method (chem-m7-p01, the next video, which owns C7-IQ2-02); sigma and pi orbital language (site lesson 4 marks it beyond the syllabus; the term "pi bond" is not used, see Open decisions); restricted rotation and cis/trans (not in the 2017 syllabus); naming rules (chem-m7-c01); isomer types (chem-m7-c02; one callback only); reactions of the double bond (chem-m7-c04a); obtaining hydrocarbons from the Earth and fractional distillation (C7-IQ2-06, chem-m7-c07; the column plate is not used here); safe handling (C7-IQ2-05, the P videos' risk tables); functional groups beyond hydrocarbons.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer. Colour key as chem-m7-c01: carbon ink; hydrogens soft grey; main chain pale blue; branches amber; double and triple bonds teal; bonding-direction lobes violet with navy angle arcs; covalent bonds solid ink; dispersion forces dotted pale-blue flicker lines; hydrogen bonds in water dotted violet (as chem-m7-c02). Board layout (constant): top-left the short task line or chip; centre the model board, one molecule or one comparison at a time; the boiling point strip at the right only in scenes 9 to 11; plates small at the left or right only in scenes 1, 9, 10, 12 and 18. Clutter rule: at most three text items bright at once; every label fades when its sentence ends; the previous case leaves before the next one draws. Reuse: painted plate `m7-camping-gas-burner-v1.png` (inspected 21 Oct: a lit blue camping stove on an unlabelled blue gas canister, silver pot supports, brass valve, blue flame; no person or hand, no text; 2000 × 2000; hook, scene 10's callback and handoff, small, never stretched). Considered, not used: `m7-crude-oil-barrel-v1.png` (inspected: a plain dark steel drum; carries no structure idea), `m7-fractional-distillation-column-v1.png` (inspected: a steel column with copper trays and side outlets; it belongs to C7-IQ2-06 in chem-m7-c07, and using it here would add a second question), `m7-oil-gas-rig-v1.png` (inspected: an offshore platform; same reason). New plates: `m7-paraffin-candle-v1.png` (hook, scene 9, handoff) and `m7-hexane-water-heptane-tubes-v1.png` (scene 12); see Assets. No human figures.
